summary: Sally Mellick Cutler is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1993. She served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1997).

Salomon Lefmann (1831–1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Berlin (Ph.D. ~1864) and attended Münster, Paris, and Heidelberg. He taught Sanskrit at Heidelberg University as an associate professor (1870) and honorary professor (1901).

Saloni Mathur works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Her career includes posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she was Associate Professor of Art History (attested 2011) and later Professor of Modern & Contemporary South Asian Art and Department Chair.

Sam van Schaik (born 1972) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Manchester (~2000). He held posts at the British Library, heading the Endangered Archives Programme (1999), and SOAS.
Samani Pratibha Pragya is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at SOAS University of London and later worked there as a research assistant (attested 2020).
Sambhavi Ganesh is a scholar in Indology who has been a doctoral student at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Radhika Govinda (attested 2026).

Samdong Rinpoche (born 1939) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as principal (attested 1980) and later as director (attested 1992).

Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti (born 1940) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He has held positions at the University of Calcutta and served as a Professor (Special Invitee) at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Sampan Chakrabarty is an Indology scholar who conducted doctoral research under Pallab Sengupta. Chakrabarty has served as a Research Scholar/Fellow at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay (born 1936) works in Tibetology and religious studies. After earning a PhD at the University of London under David Snellgrove, he held posts at SOAS, Collège de France, CNRS (Director of Research 1980), and was IATS President (1995–2000).

Samuel Beal (1825–1889) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Cambridge and Durham. He served as headmaster at Bramham College (1848–1850) and as Professor of Chinese at University College London (1877; University of London ~1877–1889).
Samuel Johnson (1709–1784) was a scholar in linguistics who was educated at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College in Stourbridge, and Pembroke College, Oxford (1728–1731).

Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Central Asian, Sinological, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West (attested 1980).
Samuel Wells Williams (1812–1884) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1831–1832) and held a post at Yale University (~1877–1884).

Sandra A. Wawrytko specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She has held posts at San Diego State University, serving as Professor (attested 1999) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2014).
Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and subsequently held a post there.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where she was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes and taught by Anne MacDonald.
Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under Sanghasena Singh (attested 1995). Sun held a post as Lecturer at Uiduk University (attested 1995).

Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tengtho Goenpa and the Institute of Language and Culture Studies. He taught at ILCS and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.

Sangharakshita (1925–2018) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1950) under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap and Dhardo Rinpoche, and founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.
